note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3616 / 出力 2322 トークン

data.question: Should we adopt the rule change block_k 3 → 2 (evict parked robots earlier) even though companies B and C voted against it, or keep the current rules (v1) for another period?
data.background: Option 1 passes check, the constitution and the KPI conditions, and it improves the main goal on_time_deliveries by +7.2 on 5/5 seeds. However, B and C voted it down, so the company vote fails. Whether customer gains justify overriding the companies is a judgment between parties that I should not make myself. In D1 you rejected a similar change because nobody had yet tried to win B and C's agreement, and you said option 1 would be revisited with an explicit decision on the vote. That decision is now needed.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 3 → 2. Per the table: on-time rises from 216.6 to 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds), late falls from 11.4 to 4.2, p95_wait_s falls from 138 to 110, blocked s falls from 1824 to 936, lowest on-time rate rises from 0.93 to 0.97 and unfinished stays at 0.0. Road violations rise from 19.0 to 28.0. Utility moves from 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8 to 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3. Adopting it overrides the votes of B and C (A ○, B ×, C ×).
options.stakeholders: Customers gain: more deliveries on time, far fewer late, shorter tail waits, and no contract change. Company A gains (+3.6 utility). Company C loses heavily (-9.5, about 14% of its utility). Company B loses slightly (-3.0). Other road users may be affected by more road violations (+9.0). Company trust in the vote process may suffer from an override.

options.summary: Stay at v1. On-time stays at 216.6, late at 11.4, p95_wait_s at 138, blocked s at 1824 and road violations at 19.0. Utility stays 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8. No vote is overridden.
options.stakeholders: Companies B and C keep their current utility, and C avoids its large loss. Company A forgoes its gain. Customers keep bearing about 7 more late deliveries per period and longer tail waits (p95 138 vs 110) for at least one more period. This is the second period in which this known cost is accepted.

recommendation.reason: The customer gains are large, consistent (5/5 seeds) and come from real service improvement: blocked time halves and p95 wait falls, not a redefinition of 'on time'. The contract is unchanged, so customers get these gains at no cost to their promises. C's loss is smaller in relative terms than in period 1 (about 14% vs about a third). Rejecting a second time would repeat a known cost to customers, who have no vote. Road violations rising from 19.0 to 28.0 is the main non-company cost and should be watched. If you prefer not to override, keep and use this period to negotiate with B and C, for example a compensating rule for C.
assumptions: The re-measured period-2 results will hold in the next period, as F2.D1.f1 showed reproducibility for the earlier measurement.
The extra road violations are not safety-critical and stay within constitutional limits (the constitution check passed).
B and C will not change their behavior strongly, for example by withdrawing robots, in response to an override.
max_wait_s is not worsened, though it is not shown in the table.

unknowns: Whether B and C would accept the change with compensation or a modified rule (e.g. a different block_k or exemptions), since no negotiation has been attempted or measured.
How B and C will adapt their robot policies after an override, and whether that erodes the measured gains.
Why C is hurt so much (which robots or routes) and whether a targeted rule could reduce its loss.
What the extra road violations mean for safety and for other road users.
How customers perceive the change; only aggregate metrics are measured, not satisfaction.
max_wait_s under option 1, which is not in the table.
Next period's demand level and whether the gains scale with it.
Long-term effects on company cooperation and on future votes if a vote is overridden.
